C1.worst_defect: The home page never shows the till itself: the hero is a headline, a paragraph and four equal-weight buttons ('Live demo', 'Quick start', 'Try with your store', 'GitHub'), two of which ('Quick start' and 'Try with your store') look like the same next step, and the first visual below them is ten text-only grey cards. Next to Shopify POS or Square, a buyer cannot see in five seconds what the cashier screen looks like.
C1.where: home.desktop.01 hero and 'What it does today'; home.phone.01

C2.worst_defect: The two strongest proof claims, 'Our acceptance run makes 25 sales, 20 of them offline, and checks that Vendure holds exactly 25 orders' and 'The same sale sent 200 times makes one order', link to nothing: no test file, no CI run, no repo path. Nothing on the site says who maintains the project or whether any shop runs it in production, and nothing says who should not use it (for example, a shop that needs refunds or integrated card terminals today).
C2.where: home.desktop.01, cards 'Keeps selling offline' and 'Every sale lands once'; tech.json home links (no test or CI link)

C3.worst_defect: Step 3 of the quick start makes the developer write two throwaway TypeScript entry files that call generateMigration and runMigrations, and run them 'with your project's existing TypeScript runner', which never names a command. It then sends the simpler bundled-migration route to 'the README' rather than the Plugin setup page that documents it. The Node requirement '^20.19 || >=22.12' is given only on Plugin setup, never in the quick start's prerequisites.

C4.worst_defect: The docs disagree on the minimum plugin version. Troubleshooting says that for 'plugin is missing or out of date' you should 'Run plugin 0.1.0 or later'; the quick start says the same message means the store 'must advertise order.create v4 and register v1'; the docs install @0.3.0, and the changelog says 0.3.0 adds order.create v5. The changelog also cites '(ADR 0005)', '(#116)' and '(#117)' as plain, unlinked text.
C4.where: text/troubleshooting.txt 'Act on a header notice'; quick-start.desktop.04 '9. Troubleshoot'; changelog.desktop.01

C5.worst_defect: The home page is a wall of ten identical bordered grey text cards followed by a plain table, with no product screenshot, illustration or icon anywhere. On the docs pages the grey sidebar panel stops at about y=900 while the page goes on, leaving a lighter band under the sidebar.
C5.where: home.desktop.01 card grid; quick-start.desktop.01 and docs.desktop.01 sidebar bottom edge

C6.worst_defect: The tax-strategy table on the quick start breaks code identifiers mid-word on phone: 'taxOptions.orderTa / xCalculationStrateg / y' and 'OrderLevelTaxCalcul / ationStrategy()'. Most TypeScript blocks are cut off at the right edge ('@vendurepos/', 'AddVendu', 'process.exitCode' hidden), so they need sideways scrolling.
C6.where: quick-start.phone.05 and quick-start.phone.06 (table); quick-start.phone.02 and quick-start.phone.03 (code blocks)

C7.worst_defect: The 404 page reuses the home page's meta description ('Open-source point of sale for Vendure. Sell from the browser...'). The share card is text only, with a hollow circle as its logo. Every docs search result's breadcrumb is just 'VendurePOS', and the results return raw markdown backticks around inline code ('`/tally/v1/commands`').

overall_worst.defect: The site's whole case against established tills rests on offline selling and exactly-once delivery, but the evidence ('Our acceptance run makes 25 sales, 20 of them offline...', 'The same sale sent 200 times makes one order') is unlinked prose. Nothing shows the till, who maintains it, or anyone running it, so I could not advise a client to trust it over Square or Shopify POS on this site's word.
overall_worst.where: home.desktop.01, cards 'Keeps selling offline' and 'Every sale lands once'
overall_worst.fix: Link each of those two claims to the actual acceptance test and a recent CI run in vendurepos/app. Put one real screenshot of the till in the hero.
